name: Risperidone
sections: Developed by Janssen in the late 1980s; one of the first second-generation (atypical) antipsychotics after clozapine. First approval/introduction: US FDA 1993 (Janssen Pharmaceutica).

Potent antagonist of serotonin 5-HT2A and dopamine D2 receptors; also blocks alpha-1, alpha-2 adrenergic and H1 histamine receptors. Balanced 5-HT2/D2 antagonism improves positive and negative symptoms with fewer extrapyramidal effects at usual doses. Receptor / target profile: Potent 5-HT2A antagonist (Ki 0.17 nM) and D2 antagonist (Ki 3.57 nM), with relatively strong 5-HT2A over D2 preference; also blocks alpha-1, alpha-2 and H1 receptors.
Summary: Well absorbed (bioavailability ~70%); Tmax ~1 h. Metabolised by CYP2D6 to 9-hydroxyrisperidone (paliperidone), which is equally active. Active-moiety half-life ~20 h. Renally excreted.
